reports.text: Bilateral 3D screening mammogram. Compared with January 2025 and earlier. Breast tissue is scattered fibroglandular. No suspicious masses, calcifications or areas of distortion. No change.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Next screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Reminder: Stool Test Kit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Julie, our records show the colon screening kit you took home in December hasn't come back to the lab yet. If you've misplaced it, reply here and we'll mail a new one.

reports.text: Real-time ultrasound of the thyroid and central neck. Right lobe: a 2.0 cm solid hypoechoic nodule with irregular margins and punctate microcalcifications. Remainder of the right lobe, the isthmus and the left lobe are of normal size and homogeneous echotexture without other nodules. No abnormal-appearing cervical lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 2.0 cm solid, hypoechoic right thyroid nodule with irregular margins and microcalcifications, highly suspicious (ACR TI-RADS TR5). Fine-needle aspiration recommended.

documents.title: Endocrinology New Patient Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Visit date: 03/02/2026
Self-referred. Copy to primary care physician.

Reason for visit: lump in the neck.

History: 46-year-old woman, a teacher, who found a lump low on the right side of her neck about a month ago while getting ready for work. It does not hurt. She has a feeling of fullness there and now and then food seems to catch on the way down. Her voice is unchanged, and she has noticed no change in weight, appetite or energy. Past history includes irritable bowel syndrome, worked up in December 2024 for fatigue and bloating. Cesarean section at 32.

Medications: polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: a maternal aunt had papillary thyroid cancer. Father with hypertension, mother with osteoporosis.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Firm, non-tender nodule of about 2 cm in the right thyroid lobe, moves with swallowing. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Otherwise normal.

Labs today: TSH 2.5 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 1.2 ng/dL (0.8-1.8). Euthyroid.

Imaging: ultrasound in clinic today shows a 2 cm solid hypoechoic nodule in the right lobe with irregular margins and microcalcifications.

Assessment: right thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features for malignancy, normal thyroid function, family history of papillary thyroid cancer.

Plan: ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration next week; she is scheduled for 3/10. Results and next steps to follow.

documents.title: Your Endocrinology Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, the endocrinology note from Monday came in. I'm sorry you've been dealing with this; you could have messaged me first, but it sounds like you're in good hands and the biopsy is the right next step. Let me know what it shows or if you want to talk anything through.

documents.title: RE: Your Endocrinology Visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. My aunt went through this so I just called them directly, didn't want to wait. Biopsy is Tuesday. I'll keep you posted.

documents.title: Pharmacy Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pharmacist called. Pt filled levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, calcitriol 0.25 mcg BID and calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID on 4/14, prescribed by a general surgeon. Pharmacist asked whether we wanted anything changed and wanted to be sure she knows to take the levothyroxine at least 4 hours apart from calcium. We had no record of surgery.

Called pt. She had a total thyroidectomy on 4/13 at a regional hospital, home the next day. Says the biopsy in March came back suspicious and the surgeon recommended taking the whole thyroid. She is taking levothyroxine first thing on an empty stomach and the calcium with meals; reviewed spacing. Post-op visit with surgery is 4/27. Some numbness around her mouth on and off since she got home; told her to call surgery today about that and to go to the ED for muscle spasms or cramping that won't stop. She agrees.

Records request (op note, pathology, discharge summary) faxed to the hospital. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Update after surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to update you. Saw the surgeon Monday. The tingling in my lips and fingers was my calcium being low, it was 7.0. They said the parathyroid glands aren't working right after the surgery and doubled the calcitriol to 0.5 twice a day, same calcium and same thyroid pill. Had blood drawn again today at their office. Pathology was papillary cancer, small, they said they got it all and the lymph nodes were clear. Endocrinology will manage everything from here. Still tired and my hands cramp sometimes but better than last week.

documents.title: RE: Update after surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Julie, and I'm glad the nodes were clear. Low calcium after thyroid surgery is common, and following it closely with surgery and endocrinology is exactly right. If the cramping or tingling gets worse, or your hands or face start to spasm, go to the ED. We've asked the hospital for your operative and pathology reports. Rest up.

documents.title: General Surgery Postoperative Visit
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
GENERAL SURGERY - POSTOPERATIVE FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 04/27/2026

Indication and course: Right thyroid nodule, TR5 on ultrasound; FNA 03/10/2026 at an outside endocrinology office read as suspicious for papillary thyroid carcinoma. Total thyroidectomy 04/13/2026, uneventful in hospital, discharged 04/14 on levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, calcium carbonate 1250 mg three times daily with meals and calcitriol 0.25 mcg twice daily.

Pathology: papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic type, 1.9 cm, right lobe. Margins negative. No extrathyroidal extension. No lymphovascular invasion. Central lymph nodes 0/3.

Interval: Two weeks of worsening tiredness, occasional difficulty swallowing, and tingling around the lips and at the fingertips. Intermittent calf cramping. Her throat feels tight when she talks for a long stretch. Over the last three days it all gets worse when she is up and moving. Denies lightheadedness, palpitations, or any recent stomach bug.

Medications: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily; calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID with meals; calcitriol 0.25 mcg BID; polyethylene glycol 3350 17 g daily as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: noncontributory.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: Mildly anxious. Incision healing well, no hematoma or seroma. Intermittent twitching of the hand muscles while she talks. Cranial nerves II-XII intact; strength full; occasional involuntary contraction of the hands.

Labs today: calcium 7.0 mg/dL, phosphate 5.6 mg/dL, magnesium 1.8 mEq/L.

Assessment: Postprocedural hypoparathyroidism after total thyroidectomy, symptomatic. Papillary thyroid carcinoma, low risk, resected.

Plan:
1. Calcitriol increased to 0.5 mcg twice daily. Continue calcium carbonate 1250 mg TID with meals and levothyroxine 112 mcg daily.
2. Repeat calcium at our office within the week.
3. Endocrinology to assume long-term management of calcium and thyroid hormone replacement.
4. Emergency evaluation for carpopedal spasm, worsening cramps, or throat tightness.
cc: primary care physician (sent on request)

documents.title: Records Status
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Surgery office faxed their 4/27 follow-up note after our second request; it includes the biopsy and pathology summary. Operative report and discharge summary still not received from the hospital. Scanned for PCP review.

documents.title: Endo visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update. Saw endocrinology last Monday. Calcium is back up to the low end of normal and they're keeping me on the same calcitriol, calcium and thyroid doses. Feeling a lot more like myself, no more tingling. Do I need to come in before school starts?

documents.title: RE: Endo visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. No need to come in before September unless something changes. Could you ask the endocrinology office to send us their notes? We didn't get one from this visit. Your physical is due in December and we'll catch up on everything then.
